title: What the Body Still Carries
logline: As an elder's hearing fades, a tea-estate family finds new ways to reach her, notes, gestures, faces turned toward her before speaking, and the household relearns, together, how she now takes in the world.
human_question: When one of the senses weakens, how does a person's whole way of taking in the world, and their family's way of reaching them, actually change?

premise.story: A multi-generation family in a hill-country tea estate community adapts as an elder gradually loses her hearing, developing new habits of communication and closeness.
premise.place: A family home in a hill-country tea estate community.
premise.experience: The viewer watches ordinary daily communication slowly change shape, and comes to notice how much of connection depends on which senses are actually working, and how a family adapts without fuss.

concept_links.why: The source holds that mental life, for beings like us, always depends on a physical base, a working sense organ for each sense, a shared base for most other mental activity [C037-P:L27; C037-M:L11]. An elder's changing hearing is a real, human instance of what happens when one of those bases weakens.

The source's account of the ear's sensitivity as a distinct, fine door, separate from the visible ear itself, frames why hearing loss is not simply about the outer ear but about a much finer threshold.

The source lists hearing what others say among the causes that set off a person's inner life [C048-M:L5]. Watching a family invent new, non-auditory ways to reach an elder shows what has to be rebuilt when that channel narrows.

what_camera_could_observe: Ordinary daily routines: meals, chores, the estate's rhythms
Written notes, gestures, a grandchild learning to face the elder when speaking
Moments of misunderstanding, correction, and laughter
The elder's own account of how her experience of the household has changed
New habits the family has built without being asked to
what_must_be_real: The elder's clear, ongoing, informed consent, separate from the family's; no framing that turns her hearing loss into a moral lesson or links it to any claim about spiritual attainment.

possible_arc.opening: An ordinary day in the household, hearing loss already part of daily life.
possible_arc.turn: A moment of real miscommunication, and the family's real way of working through it.
possible_arc.ending_open: The household's adapted rhythm, whatever it actually looks like, closes the film.

position_hint: middle: a tender, domestic film set in a working tea-estate community, giving the group a hill-country, multi-generational setting.

requirements: A multi-generation household in a tea-estate community, with an elder and family willing to be filmed
The elder's own clear, separate, ongoing consent
Enough time on location to observe real adaptation, not a single staged demonstration

suggestions.name: A tea-estate community in the central hill country
suggestions.region: Nuwara Eliya or Hatton area, Central Province
suggestions.why: Well-established tea-estate communities with multi-generation households.
suggestions.access_notes: Estate management permission may be needed alongside the family's own consent.
suggestions.verify: A specific family and their willingness to be filmed are unconfirmed.

risks: Pity-framing of a vulnerable elder rather than showing her agency
The elder's dignity and clear, separate consent must come before the family's
Implying any link between hearing loss and the source's doctrinal claims about spiritual capacity, which must never be suggested about a real person
drop_if: The elder does not clearly and separately consent, even if the family agrees
The family does not want their adaptation shown on camera
The story cannot be told without exploiting a vulnerable person's condition

connections.note: Both are studies of the senses at work, one where several combine in a skilled trade, one where a household adapts as one of them weakens.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
